request.spec:
Show the policy versions: one line per version, oldest first, as <version> <from or start>
<key>=<value> <count of claims whose policy version it is>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the policy versions: one line per version, oldest first, as <version> <from or start>
<key>=<value> <count of claims whose policy version it is>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The policy versions are now shown on screen, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec (the main test and scenarios 1–3).

**The change**
- **Stored data:** each policy version now keeps the value it set. A new migration, `V126__policy_version_value.sql`, adds the column and fills it in for existing versions. `PolicyVersion`, `Sheet.record` and the saved history snapshots (`SheetHistory`) carry the value too.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{id}/policy-versions`, returns the versions oldest first. Each comes with how many of the sheet's claims fall under it, meaning it is the version in force on the claim's date.
- **Front end:** a new "Policy versions" section on the home screen has a `policy-show` button. Pressing it lists one `policy-line` per version, as `<version> <from> <key>=<value> <count>`. A setting saved without a from-date is already stored from the sheet's today, so it shows that date; "start" only appears if a version has no date at all.

**Three other fixes the spec needed.** These change existing behaviour outside the listing:
1. **"Terms in force" display:** it now stays empty until a terms value is recorded for the sheet's today, the same way floor and late percent already work. Before, it showed the default of 14.
2. **Adding a claim:** a DRAFT whose due-by falls inside a closed period can now be added; opening it is still refused. The add method's own comment already said this, but the code refused it. I removed that check in `ClaimService.add`.
3. **Bulk grade change:** it now records the grade even when the person already has it, as the person form does. Before, giving Ben grade B when he was already B left nothing in his timeline.

If anything relied on the old behaviour in those three places, it will now act differently.

I didn't touch the test spec, `bin/*`, `e2e/support` or the docs, and I removed the temporary debug spec I'd used to find the failures.
